title: Pair Sum
hints: Brute force is two nested loops. Interviewers will ask you to beat O(n²).
As you walk the array, store value → index. The partner you need is target − current.
Look up the partner before inserting the current value so you never reuse an index.

title: Seen Before
hints: Sorting then scanning neighbors is O(n log n).
A set of seen values is O(n) time and answers in one pass.

title: Letter Twins
hints: If the lengths differ, they cannot be anagrams.
Count letters in s, decrement with t, confirm the map is all zeros — or sort both strings.

title: Cluster Anagrams
hints: Two words are anagrams if their sorted characters match — that sorted string is a map key.
A 26-length frequency tuple is a faster key than sorting each word.

title: Top K Frequent
hints: Count frequencies first.
A min-heap of size k, or bucket sort by frequency, beats a full sort.

title: Mirror String
hints: Two pointers: skip junk on the left and right, then compare lowercase letters.
Do not allocate a filtered copy if you can skip in place — interviewers notice extra memory.

title: Three Sum
hints: Sort first. Fix one number, then two-pointer the rest toward zero.
Skip duplicate values at all three indices or you will emit duplicate triplets.

title: Max Water
hints: Start at both ends. The width only shrinks, so you must raise the limiting (shorter) side.
Move the pointer at the shorter line inward. Prove why the other move cannot beat the current best.

title: Buy Once, Sell Once
hints: Track the lowest price so far and the best price - lowest as you scan.
You cannot sell before you buy — a single left-to-right pass is enough.

title: Longest Unique Window
hints: Grow a right pointer. When you see a duplicate, advance left past the previous copy.
Store last-seen index in a map so left can jump, not crawl.

title: Minimum Covering Window
hints: Need a countdown of how many unique chars in t are currently satisfied.
Expand right to make the window valid, then shrink left as far as it stays valid.

title: Bracket Stack
hints: Push openers. On a closer, the stack top must be the matching opener.
The stack must be empty at the end.

title: Next Warmer Day
hints: A monotonic decreasing stack of indices: pop when today's temp is warmer.
Distance is i − popped_index.

title: Search a Rotated Array
hints: One half of [lo, hi] is always sorted. Check whether target lives in that half.
Decide which pointer to move by comparing nums[mid] with nums[lo] (or nums[hi]).

title: Reverse the Chain
hints: Iterative: prev = None, walk cur, flip cur.next to prev.
Recursive: reverse the tail, then head.next.next = head; head.next = None.

title: Cycle Detect
hints: A set of seen nodes is the obvious solution.
Floyd: slow moves 1, fast moves 2. If they meet, there is a cycle.

title: Invert Tree
hints: If the node is null, return it. Otherwise swap children, then recurse.
BFS with a queue also works — same swap at every node.

title: Level Order
hints: BFS. Snapshot queue length at the start of each level.
Do not mix next-level nodes into the current list.

title: LCA in a BST
hints: If both p and q are less than root, go left. Both greater, go right. Otherwise root is the split.
This is O(h), not a full tree walk.

title: Island Count
hints: Scan every cell. When you find a '1', increment the count and sink the whole island.
Sinking is DFS/BFS to all 4-neighbors, flipping them to '0'.

title: Course Order
hints: This is cycle detection in a directed graph.
Kahn's algorithm (indegree queue) or DFS coloring both work.

title: Climb Steps
hints: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). That is Fibonacci.
You only need the last two values — O(1) extra memory.

title: Rob Houses
hints: For each house: skip it (keep prev best) or rob it (prev-prev + this house).
dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]).

title: Coin Change
hints: dp[x] = min coins to make x. dp[0] = 0, others start at inf.
For each coin, for each x >= coin: dp[x] = min(dp[x], dp[x-coin] + 1).

title: Merge Ranges
hints: Sort by start time.
If the next start is ≤ current end, extend the end; otherwise push a new interval.
